recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow correction to the applied wording and preserves the approved FHIR-I semantics; further work is only needed if the work group later reopens the broader aggregationMode policy.
issue_request: Published FHIR-core StructureDefinition issue FHIR-26386 asked how a profile can express whether Reference.identifier may be used instead of Reference.reference. The final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution said Reference datatype constraints belong in ElementDefinition.profile, aggregationMode is about computable resolution of Reference.reference, identifier-only logical references are not expected to be computably resolvable, and the aggregation guidance should be understood in that light.
initial_application: The aggregation rules were already present from GF#14402 and state that aggregationMode requires the Reference.reference element to be present and populated. The Jira-tagged commit 50302bfe36 added FHIR-26386 logical-reference text to source/references.html, but the final clause was left malformed as 'nor does ... aggregation restrictions.'
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2020-07-06 record the 12-0-0 decision and rationale that aggregation mode is about how references resolve. A 2022 Zulip implementation thread for FHIR-26386 confirms that the aggregationMode rule already existed and only the logical-reference clarification still needed application. source/fhir.ini maps Reference to references.html and ElementDefinition to elementdefinition.html, confirming the relevant narrative pages are in current build scope.
reconciliation: Changed source/references.html to make the malformed clause grammatical: aggregation restrictions now explicitly do not apply to identifier-only logical references. No broader ElementDefinition prose was added because the existing aggregation section already provides the Reference.reference rule and the implementation thread treated that part as complete.
source_changes: source/references.html: fixed the logical references sentence so it says aggregation restrictions do not apply, instead of ending with the incomplete phrase 'nor does ... aggregation restrictions.'
